summary: Franz Boas studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Friedrich Ratzel and Wilhelm Wundt. A linguist, he worked at Clark University (~1889–1892), the Smithsonian, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (~1896–1942).

Franz Bopp worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Windischmann, Silvestre de Sacy, and Chézy at Paris and Göttingen. He served as Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867) and was a member of the Prussian Academy.

Franz Carl Christian Vorländer was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Bonn and Humboldt University under Bopp, Lachmann, and Schleiermacher. He held posts as PD at Berlin (1842) and ao. Professor at Marburg (1843).

Franz Ferdinand Schwarz studied Indology, history/archaeology, and linguistics at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein and at the Center for Hellenic Studies. He served as Professor at the University of Graz starting in 1976.

Franz Heinrich Trithen studied at Humboldt University under Bopp, Boeckh, and Lachmann, and at Oxford. Working in linguistics and Indology, he taught at Rugby School and served at the British Museum and as modern languages professor at Oxford (~1848–1851).

Franz Hessler was an Indology scholar who studied at the universities of Heidelberg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Würzburg between 1822 and 1827. In 1852, he was named an ordinary member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Franz Josef Meier earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1926–1931). Specializing in Indology and Sinology, he worked as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library from 1937 to 1970.

Franz Joseph Steingass studied at the University of Munich, working in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held posts as Professor of Modern Languages at Wakefield Grammar School and at the Oriental Institute, Woking (~1884–1890).

Franz Karl Alter was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and other fields who studied at Charles University, the University of Vienna, and under Paulinus of St. Bartholomew. He served as Vienna University Library custos (1779) and taught at Vienna (~1781–1804).

Franz Kielhorn studied Indology at Göttingen, Breslau, Berlin, Leipzig, and Oxford under Stenzler, Weber, and Benfey. He was Late Professor at Deccan College (1866–1881) and held the chair of Indology at Göttingen from 1881.

Franz Misteli, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Zurich, Bonn, Geneva, and Paris. He served as Privatdozent at the University of Bern (1873) and as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Basel (1874; 1877–1898).

Linguist Franz Nikolaus Finck studied at Munich, Paris, and Marburg. He held posts at the University of Marburg (1896), the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1903–1910), and Humboldt University of Berlin (Privatdozent in 1903, ao. Professor in 1909).

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin as PD for Oriental languages (1829) and a.o. Professor in theology (1831).

Linguist Franz Specht studied at Berlin and Leipzig under Windisch, Leskien, Brugmann, and Schulze. He was ao. Professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1923–1937), ord. Professor at Breslau (1937–1943) and Berlin (1943–1945), and Professor at Mainz (1946–1949).

Franz Valéry Marie Cumont studied religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies at Ghent under Charles Michel, as well as at Bonn, Berlin, Vienna, and Paris. He was a teacher (1892) and Professor (1906) at Ghent University.

Franz Woepcke worked in history/archaeology and linguistics, studying at Berlin and Bonn under Georg Freytag, Julius Mohl, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He served as a mathematics teacher at the Französisches Gymnasium Berlin from 1856 to 1858.

Franz Xaver Erhard studied Tibetology at Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University, Bonn, and Leipzig. He held posts at Humboldt University, Wolfson College, Oxford, Stadtmuseum Meppen, and served as Visiting Professor for Tibetology at Leipzig (2022–2023).

Franz Xaver Miklosich studied linguistics and Indology at Graz and Vienna. He served at the Austrian National Library (1844–1862) and was appointed ao. Professor of Slavic Philology and Literature at the University of Vienna in 1849.

Franz von Erdmann studied Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics at Rostock and Göttingen. He served as Privatdozent of Oriental languages at Rostock (1818) and Professor of Oriental languages at Kazan University (~1818–1845).

Franz von László, a scholar of Indology, studied philology at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1941 and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn (~1948–1952) under doctoral supervisor Willibald Kirfel.
